title: Anti-Japanese Organization Abduct 17 Chinese For Dealing With Japanese

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C & S. B. REGISTRY
No. D 4732
Date 4 / 4 / 33

FULL TRANSLATION.

SHANGHAI NICHI-NICHI. March 28, 1933.

ANTI-JAPANESE ORGANIZATION ABDUCT 17 CHINESE FOR DEALING
WITH JAPANESE.

Of late many cases of the
detention and murder of Chinese for dealing with Japanese
have occurred along the Yangtsze Valley indicating the
seriousness of the anti-Japanese movement.
Last week 17 Chinese in Shanghai,
who had business connection with Japanese, were abducted
by the Anti-Japanese Association of Shanghai and their
whereabouts are still unknown. It is reported that the
17 victims included 2 workers of the Dong Hwa Cotton Mill,
2 workers of the Nikka Cotton Mill and some workers of the
Naigai Cotton Mill, the Shanghai Cotton Mill and other
Cotton mills. For this reason the workers of all Japanese
cotton mills have become panic-stricken.
The other day the anti-Japanese
Association intimidated coolies engaged by the Mitsui Yoko
in loading coal on an American warship. The coolies
stopped the work.

A CORRECTION (April 2, 1933) the report that
The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi publishes
a correction to the effect that a number of Chinese
workers of local Japanese cotton mills had been abducted
by the anti-Japanese association, which appeared in our
issue of March 28, is denied by the Shanghai Municipal
Council.

26. (brine) CHIN

Information. Experience
in the past shows that
this correction is the fullest
satisfaction which the
Nichi Nichi is likely to give.
J. McEwen
O. i/c Sp. Br.
APR. 4 1933

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别股登记处
编号 D 4732
日期 1933年4月4日

全译文。

《上海日日新闻》。1933年3月28日。

反日组织绑架17名与日本人往来的中国人。

近来，长江流域发生多起因与日本人往来而遭拘禁和杀害中国人的案件，表明反日运动的严重性。
上周，上海有17名与日本人有业务往来的中国人被上海反日协会绑架，其下落至今不明。据报道，这17名受害者包括东华纱厂的2名工人、日华纱厂（Nikka Cotton Mill）的2名工人，以及内外棉株式会社纱厂、上海纱厂和其他一些纱厂的若干工人。因此，所有日本纱厂的工人都陷入恐慌。
日前，反日协会恐吓受三井洋行雇佣在美国军舰上装煤的苦力。苦力们停止了工作。

更正（1933年4月2日）
《上海日日新闻》刊登一则更正，称该报3月28日刊发的关于多名中国工人被反日协会绑架的报道不实，上海公共租界工部局对此予以否认。

26. (盐水) CHIN

情报。过往经验表明，
这份更正是《日日新闻》
可能给出的最充分的答复。
J. McEwen
特别股主管
1933年4月4日

ch 28, 1933.
Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

NICHI-NICHI

DRUNKEN BRITON RELIEVES NATURE AT THE JAPANESE CONSULATE

At 3.30 p.m. yesterday a drunken European aged about 24, claiming to be a British subject, alighted from a ricsha at the back gate of the Japanese Consulate and attempted to enter the gate. He was stopped by a Japanese officer guarding the gate. Then the man started to relieve nature at the gate but he was advised to go home. He refused to leave and started to create trouble. He was therefore taken to Hongkew Station by a constable of that station where the man was detained.

CHINESE MOB THREATENS JAPANESE CONSUL

At 2 p.m. yesterday Mr. Tsukamoto, Japanese Consul at Hankow, and his wife accompanied by a clerk and the latter's wife visited Chapei in a motor car under the guidance of constable Tani of the Shanghai Japanese Consular Police to inspect the war zone. Whilst they were travelling in the vicinity of Pah Tz Jao, their motor car became stuck in the mud. A number of Chinese immediately collected around the motor car in a somewhat menacing attitude. The constable quickly ran to the Paosan glass factory and from there he reported the incident to the Japanese Consular Police which immediately dispatched ten police officers to the scene. In the meantime, Mr. Tsukamoto's party had decided to abandon their motor car and were walking back to town when they were met by the Consular Party.

ANTI-JAPANESE ORGANIZATION ABDUCT 17 CHINESE FOR DEALING WITH JAPANESE

Of late many cases of the detention and murder of Chinese for dealing with Japanese have occurred along the Yangtsze Valley indicating the seriousness of the anti-Japanese movement.

Last week 17 Chinese in Shanghai, who had business connections with Japanese, were abducted by the Anti-Japanese Association of Shanghai and their whereabouts are still unknown. It is reported that the 17 victims included 2 workers of the Dong Hwa Cotton Mill, 2 workers of the Nikka Cotton Mill and some workers of the Naigai Cotton Mill, the Shanghai Cotton Mill and other Cotton mills. For this reason the workers of all Japanese cotton mills have become panic-stricken.

The other day the anti-Japanese association intimidated coolies engaged by the Mitsui Yoko in loading coal on an American warship. The coolies stopped the work.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER / Acting / (CRIME BRANCH)）
a.c. (8/4 B-)

A CORRECTION (April 2, 1933)
The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi publishes a correction to the effect that the report on the number of Chinese workers abducted, which appeared in its issue of March 28, is not correct.

1933年3月28日。
晨间译文。

杂项

《日日新闻》

醉酒英国人在日本领事馆随地便溺

昨日下午3时30分，一名自称是英国臣民、年龄约24岁的醉酒欧洲人，在日本领事馆后门下车，试图进入馆内。他被一名守卫大门的日本警官拦住。随后，该男子开始在大门口随地便溺，有人劝其回家。他拒绝离开并开始滋事。因此，他被该辖区的一名巡捕带至虹口捕房，并在那里被拘留。

中国暴民威胁日本领事

昨日下午2时，日本驻汉口领事塚本先生及其夫人在一名职员及其夫人的陪同下，在上海日本领事馆警察谷尼（Tani，音译）巡捕的引导下，乘车前往闸北视察战区。当他们行驶至八字桥附近时，汽车陷入泥中。许多中国人立即围聚在汽车周围，态度颇具威胁性。该巡捕迅速跑至宝三玻璃厂，从那里向日本领事馆警察报告了这一事件，后者随即派遣十名警员赶赴现场。与此同时，塚本先生一行决定弃车，正步行返回市区时，遇到了领事馆派出的队伍。

反日组织绑架17名与日本人往来的中国人

近来，长江流域发生多起因与日本人往来而遭拘禁和杀害中国人的案件，表明反日运动的严重性。

上周，上海有17名与日本人有业务往来的中国人被上海反日协会绑架，其下落至今不明。据报道，这17名受害者包括东华纱厂的2名工人、日华纱厂（Nikka Cotton Mill）的2名工人，以及内外棉株式会社纱厂、上海纱厂和其他一些纱厂的若干工人。因此，所有日本纱厂的工人都陷入恐慌。
日前，反日协会恐吓受三井洋行雇佣在美国军舰上装煤的苦力。苦力们停止了工作。

（印：副总监 / 代理 / （刑事股））
a.c. (8/4 B-)

更正（1933年4月2日）
《上海日日新闻》刊登一则更正，称该报3月28日刊发的关于被绑架中国工人数量的报道不正确。
